## Design

### 2026-10-08 – I started work on the PCB for my alarm clock, Meme-O-Clock.

**1.5h**

I started work on the PCB for my alarm clock, Meme-O-Clock.

This is my first time creating circuits and electrical schematics, as well as my first time using KiCad, so I'm using a Youtube tutorial and ChatGPT to guide me along the way as I design.

I started by picking which microcontroller to use, and after comparing options, I decided upon the Arduino Nano ESP32 for ease-of-use and integration with the Arduino ecosystem, which I'm already familiar with

![meme-o-clock-pcbschematic-update-10-8-26](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6HcBJbXMNK4i7wcprvAdH7WjsyHy5dnv/665e89cc62b8ba3ce657dcb0d3f53d46cae1f9de57d4b5117eb47f9d6cf9e7ad.png)

. I also decided to use a MAX98357A amplifier for my speaker, but I have not added that to my schematic yet. My OLED display and speaker will not be soldered directly onto the PCB, but rather be attached by connections from the PCB.

I continued by adding push button switches and a USB-C receptacle to my schematic. For my next session, I aim to add the MAX98357A amplifier as well as connections for my OLED display and speaker to the schematic.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/6d8b21e4-1a05-4baf-af58-6c9630de95d2/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-08 – I added the MAX98357A audio amplifier to the schematic. While wiring the SD_Mode pin, I learned more about resistors and Ohm's law. After finishing wiring on the amplifier, I add a J3 socket, meaning

**0.75h**

I added the MAX98357A audio amplifier to the schematic. While wiring the SD_Mode pin, I learned more about resistors and Ohm's law. After finishing wiring on the amplifier, I add a J3 socket, meaning the speaker connection should be complete.

### 2026-10-09 – Finished the PCB Schematic

**0.92h**

Finished the PCB Schematic

Considered adding USB-A receptacle for expansion but decided against it.

Wired up speaker and camera connectors, added light sensor and a 3 pin connector for potential expansion with a motion sensor.

Ran ERC checks, found no substantial errors.

Didn't need the tutorial this time to finish the schematic, just ChatGPT to help explain what parts do what and how to figure out pin assignments on connectors.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/432bd985-da5e-413b-b539-129427f47726/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-11 – The Meme-O-Clock PCB is almost complete.

**1.22h**

The Meme-O-Clock PCB is almost complete.

I used the Youtube Tutorial and ChatGPT a little more to help me decide which parts to use and why in order to assign all the footprints for my board.

After assigning the footprints, I moved onto the PCB layout.

I'm considering either PCBWay of JLCPCB as my manufacturer, and I'll finalize that later.

The last thing I have to do later today is debug - the DRC said I have 89 errors.

### 2026-10-11 – Struggling to wire together the PCB.

**0.8h**

Struggling to wire together the PCB.

I realized a lot of those 89 errors were missing connections because I forgot to wire everything together.
That's when I realize my current layout isn't very thoughtful when it comes to wiring.
I'll come back to finish the rest later.

### 2026-10-11 – The PCB is complete!

**1.5h**

The PCB is complete!

I forgot to turn on Timelapse while working during this, so I don't have a time lapse, but I finally finished routing all the tracks and now the PCB is ready.

I resolved all 89 errors over this last 1.5 hours, and I learned about how to use the different layers and how to use vias to make wiring much easier.

Now all that's left before having it made would be to clear manufacturing checks.
